{"world_model":"Simplest model: time ≈ fixed (~0.1 s) + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost has a pixel-proportional compute part plus a large memory-bound part on the 31×31 maps (whitening output, group 1: BN/GELU/pool). Accuracy rises slowly with total steps (~0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch, ~1.5–2.7 s/pp). Tip E036: 5.31 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Fresh seeds 13–22 gave 0.7525, so the population mean is ~0.752–0.753, only 0.2–0.3 pp over the 0.75 bar. The tip sits at the accuracy cliff.

Mechanisms:
1. Early low resolution is cheap (E026, E033). E040 (40/0/30/30) saved ~0.12 s for ~0.06 pp on seeds 0–2. The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
2. Memory-bound cuts save more than their MAC share (E028, E034, E036). The freeze at 75% with an annealed group-1 LR is nearly free. E037 shows the dose is nonlinear: a 60% freeze cost ~0.4 pp for ~0.25 s. E039 (BN fold) is not worth it. Trims in E040/E041 each saved 0.1–0.17 s but cost 0.07–0.2 pp. Time saved per trim is larger than I modelled, since the 20 px steps are cheap but fixed overheads shrink too.
3. Averaging, LS, warmup and Lookahead-interval tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032) are null or negative by 0.2–0.7 pp. The recipe is in a narrow local optimum, so shade any non-systems change by about −0.1 pp. Any RNG change re-rolls seeds 0–2, and the re-roll scatter (SE ~0.12 pp) is as large as most effects.
4. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded with batch size and an RNG re-draw (E006).
5. Systems work is worth ~1% each. Math-identical changes keep per-seed outcomes bit-identical (E035), so accuracy stays 0.7532 exactly on seeds 0–2. The remaining systems gains are ≲0.05–0.1 s each.
6. Sample dropping (E031) costs ~0.4 pp for ~0.5 s, worse than the epoch dial.

Noise: 3-seed accuracy SE ~0.1–0.15 pp. Held-out 10-seed SE ~0.06 pp. Time noise ±0.03 s. Seeds 3–12 carry a winner's curse of ~0.05–0.1 pp.

Misses: the E034, E037 and E041 times (memory-bound and small-res savings are larger than I modelled), and the accuracy cost of the deeper freeze.

forecasts.reason: Diagnostic with no recipe change; the tip result is unchanged and the profile likely shows non-GEMM kernels near 30%+ of the step.
An earlier freeze of conv1 sits on the E037 cliff side, so the accuracy loss likely exceeds the ~0.07 s saving's worth.
A 70% freeze is a small dose, saving ~0.04 s with a likely ~0.1 pp loss, which is within noise of the keep gate.
BN recalibration may add a little, but the Lookahead copy already gives a smooth average; the gain is probably under 0.15 pp.
A 16 px start with 1×1 final maps saves ~0.06 s but is likely to cost 0.1–0.2 pp, which is below the bar.
Math-identical, so accuracy is bit-identical; it saves up to ~0.03–0.05 s on the mean of trial-0 overhead.

cruxes: What is the true population mean of the tip (pooled seeds 3–22)? If it is below 0.752, every further trim is infeasible and only accuracy boosters matter.
Is any time-neutral accuracy booster (BN recalibration, wd, Muon lr, batch size 1500) worth ≥0.15 pp on held-out seeds?
Where is the freeze dose cliff (70% vs 60%), and is the loss from a lost group-1 update or from the 28 px phase?
